chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Uthina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

While the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was seated in the mosque, a man entered. He stood up and began to pray, but did not complete his ruku' nor his sujud. So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He pecked like the pecking of a crow. If this man were to die while his prayer is like this, he would surely die upon a religion other than mine.'

key_terms.رُكُوع: Ruku' — the obligatory bowing position in salat, where one bends at the waist with hands on knees
key_terms.سُجُود: Sujud — the obligatory prostration in salat, where the forehead, nose, palms, knees, and toes all touch the ground
key_terms.غَيْرِ دِينِي: Other than my religion — a declaration that such prayer does not fulfill the religious obligation
key_terms.نَقَرَ كَنَقْرِ الْغُرَابِ: Pecking like a crow — a metaphor for rapid, incomplete prostration without proper attention or stillness

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about pecking like a crow mean in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates that the Prophet (SAWW), while in the mosque, observed a man who performed his prayer hastily without completing the obligatory ruku' (bowing) and sujud (prostration). The Prophet condemned this behavior with a vivid metaphor — comparing it to a crow's rapid pecking — and issued a severe warning: such a person dies outside Islam. This hadith emphasizes that the physical acts of prayer must be performed completely and attentively, as cutting them short invalidates the prayer and constitutes a grave religious failure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘While Rasool-Allahsaww was seated in the Masjid when a man entered. So he stood and prayed Salāt, and hesaww neither completed his Rukū nor his Sajdah. So hesaww said: ‘He pecks the like pecking of the crow. If this one were to die and this is how his Salāt is, he would have died upon other than mysaww Religion’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following:

“A man entered the Masjid when the Messenger of Allah was present. He began to perform Salah (prayer) without properly doing Ruku‘ and Sajdah. He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘He acted like a crow picking up grain from the ground. If he dies with his Salah (prayer) of such condition he dies in a religion other than my religion.’”
